Subject: Deal-Tethered Provisioning Queue & OEM Quote Negotiation

Team —

Mayfield is asking for a committed onboarding window tied to the RD-2027-4589 deal. They need 1200 A100-equivalent slots (burstable) across a 6–9 month ramp with a hard requirement: dedicated pool availability by the time of go-live (Q2 window for them).

Attached is their formal req sheet. High-level asks:
- Harmonized OEM quotes (unit + lead time + allocation lane)
- Cloud backstop options if OEM fulfilment slips (temporary reserved instances / committed cloud capacity)
- Chunked delivery options (tranche-based provisioning so they can start earlier)

Can Karthik/Ben coordinate vendor asks (OmniGPU + AcmeCloud) and get draft term/lead-time language we can present to legal? Marissa — if we can get a short MOP (mutual action plan) by EOD Friday, that helps sales close the contingent SKU approval.

Attachment: Mayfield_Req_2027-4589.xlsx

Thanks,
Mateo
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Deal-Tethered Provisioning Queue & OEM Quote Negotiation

Hi Mateo / Marissa —

Thanks for the context and the req sheet. Quick notes from AcmeCloud:
- We can provide a committed reserve (monthly committed instances) as a backstop for Mayfield while OEM allocation completes. Lead time to stand up reserve: ~10 business days once contract is signed.
- Opex vs Capex trade: committed reserves reduce unit cost but require a 3–6 month minimum term in our standard marketplace terms (see attached AcmeCloud_Commit_Terms.docx).

Elliott (OmniGPU) — can you confirm the current OEM allocation lane and estimated shipment cadence for 1200 A100-equivalent units? If OEM has tranche windows, we need the first tranche to cover the customer's pilot.

—Chris
Chris Lin
Strategic Cloud Sales
AcmeCloud

> Thanks for the context and the req sheet. Quick notes from AcmeCloud:
> - We can provide a committed reserve ...

Mateo/Team —

Short answer: OEM allocation is under pressure but we have a feasible path. Current status:
- Allocation lane: Q1/Q2 tranche windows. First tranche (pilot) feasible within 8–10 weeks if PO is received by Dec 15; second tranche follows ~10–12 weeks after first.
- Lead time per unit: 10–14 weeks typical, but our negotiated program for Redwood customers can move several hundred units earlier if we get a deposit / PO and can prioritize on manufacturer lines.
- SKU substitutions: we can swap in an equivalent 80GB variant for the earliest tranche with a 6–8 week lead, but pricing and perf delta will need to be documented.

We attached a revised OmniGPU_Quote_v2.pdf with tranche pricing and an allocation-lane memo. Miguel (ops) will need the MOP timeline to align our staging pool.

Attachment: OmniGPU_Quote_v2.pdf

Best,
Elliott Reyes
Head of Allocations
OmniGPU

Subject: Re: Deal-Tethered Provisioning Queue & OEM Quote Negotiation

Elliott — thanks. A few clarifying asks (so legal and procurement can draft precise CTAs):
- Please convert the tranche language into a firm ETA window per tranche (e.g., tranche 1: shipment w/in 8–10 weeks from PO receipt). We need explicit calendar ranges for the MOP.
- Confirm whether the deposit triggers allocation prioritization and if that deposit is refundable in case of delays.
- If we take the SKU substitution path for tranche 1, provide a short perf-impact blurb we can include in the sales deck.

Karthik / Ben — can you prepare a short procurement ask packet for OmniGPU with: PO template, deposit T&Cs, acceptance criteria? I'll draft the MOP and loop legal for the fallback clauses (cloud backstop + tranche SLAs).

Thanks — Mateo

Team / Rachel —

Summarizing next steps so Mayfield has a single view (this will be the MOP we present to them):
1) Procurement packet: Redwood to send PO template + deposit T&Cs to OmniGPU (action: Karthik / Ben) — target: 12/08.
2) OEM tranche ETAs: OmniGPU to provide calendar windows by EOD 12/06 and confirm refundability on deposits (action: Elliott).
3) Cloud backstop: AcmeCloud to prepare committed reserve terms and a timeline to activate (action: Chris) — deliverable: AcmeCloud_Commit_Terms.docx.
4) Customer sign-off: Rachel to confirm appetite for SKU substitution on pilot tranche (action: Rachel) — target: 12/09.

HubSpot / docs: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345 | Mayfield request folder: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/req-2027-4589

If all look good, operations (Miguel) will start reserving a staging pool upon receipt of the PO; legal will draft fallback language around tranche SLAs and cloud failover.
